An odd-eyed cat has one blue eye and one eye either green, yellow, amber, or brown. This is a feline form of complete heterochromia,[1][2] a condition that occurs in some other animals, including humans. There is also sectoral (partial) heterochromia, where two different colours occur within the same iris. The condition most commonly affects solid white cats, but may be found in cats of any coat colour.[3][4][5]. The odd-eyed colouring is caused when either the epistatic (recessive) white gene or dominant white (which masks any other colour genes and turns a cat completely solid white)[3] or the white spotting gene (which is the gene responsible for bicolour coats)[4] prevents melanin (pigment)  development, resulting in a cat with one blue eye and one green, yellow, amber, or brown eye.
